provenance_source_judgement.keyed_off: candidate row (candidates.producer, plus candidates.state as the declared verdict)
provenance_source_judgement.reasoning: A claim's standing is an assessment property. candidates.producer records who mined/declared the candidate; verdicts.producer records who assessed the claim, and the store now has that column. Nothing writes candidates.state from a verdict (writers are insert_candidate and the producer declaration at store.py:409), so the declared CONFIRMS is a mining/curation declaration, not an assessment.
provenance_source_judgement.consequence_if_wrong: Residual fail-open on the model-mined path: a candidate with producer='model' and state='confirmed' still renders CONFIRMS with zero verdict rows (the authoritative store has 0 verdicts today), so U5.13's stated invariant is not closed for model-mined claims; and the mirror false negative caps a genuinely model-assessed claim (verdicts.producer='model', CONFIRMS) to EXTENDS when its candidate is replay/fixture. The real docket is safe only because its candidate is replay-sourced.
